name: com.whatthescopeshows/simulator
title: What the Scope Shows
description: Simulated telescope eyepiece views, magnification and field math, and type advice for beginners

tools.name: view_target
tools.description: A picture of what the Moon, Jupiter, Saturn, the Orion Nebula (M42) or the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) looks like through one of 13 teaching telescopes, as a schematic eyepiece sketch, with the magnification, true field of view, exit pupil, a short description and the simulator page that draws the same view. Give a teaching scope, or your own aperture and focal length for the numbers. Pictures exist for the default teaching combinations; other settings still get the numbers and the simulator link. Cite and link the returned url.

target.description: Moon, Jupiter, Saturn, M42 (Orion Nebula) or M31 (Andromeda Galaxy). Common names work.

scope.description: A teaching scope: an id from list_targets, or words like "8-inch Dobsonian", "70 mm refractor", "8-inch SCT" or "10x50 binoculars".

aperture_mm.description: Your own aperture in mm, with focal_length_mm, instead of a teaching scope.

focal_length_mm.description: Your own focal length in mm, with aperture_mm.

eyepiece_mm.description: Eyepiece focal length in mm. The teaching eyepieces are 32, 25, 20, 10 and 6 mm. Ignored for binoculars.

sky.description: Sky brightness: city, mixed or dark (Bortle 8, 5 or 3), or a Bortle class from 1 to 9.

seeing_arcsec.description: Seeing (atmospheric blur) in arcseconds, 0.5 to 5. Pictures exist for 1.5 only.

include_image.description: Also send the picture itself as image content, not only its url.

tools.name: choose_beginner_scope
tools.description: The telescope type (refractor, Dobsonian, Schmidt-Cassegrain or binoculars) the What the Scope Shows chooser recommends for a budget, target, portability and sky, with its reasons, a matching simulator view and the type page. Same rules as the chooser page. It recommends a type, never a brand or model. Cite and link the returned url.

budget.description: under-300, 300-700, 700-1500 or over-1500 (US dollars), or an amount such as 450.

targets.description: planets (Moon and planets), deepsky (clusters, nebulae, galaxies), both, or unsure.

portability.description: grab (grab-and-go, apartment or travel), yard (can carry a tube and base to the yard), or fixed (can stay put in a backyard).

sky.description: Sky brightness: city, mixed or dark (Bortle 8, 5 or 3), or a Bortle class from 1 to 9.

tools.name: recommend_eyepiece
tools.description: Which of the five teaching eyepieces (32, 25, 20, 10 or 6 mm) suits a target in a teaching telescope, with the magnification and field it gives, whether a Barlow would help, and the eyepieces guide, magnification guide and simulator page to cite. Teaching presets only, not a shopping list. Cite and link the returned url.

scope.description: A teaching scope: an id from list_targets, or words like "8-inch Dobsonian", "70 mm refractor", "8-inch SCT" or "10x50 binoculars".

target.description: Moon, Jupiter, Saturn, M42 (Orion Nebula) or M31 (Andromeda Galaxy). Common names work.

sky.description: Sky brightness: city, mixed or dark (Bortle 8, 5 or 3), or a Bortle class from 1 to 9.

seeing_arcsec.description: Seeing (atmospheric blur) in arcseconds, 0.5 to 5. Pictures exist for 1.5 only.

tools.name: explain_term
tools.description: The plain-language explanation, and the formula where there is one, for a telescope term the site explains: magnification, focal ratio, exit pupil, true field of view, apparent field, field stop, Dawes and Rayleigh resolution, useful magnification, light grasp, limiting magnitude, Bortle, seeing, surface brightness, central obstruction, image orientation, Barlow, collimation, eyepieces and mounts. Cite and link the returned url.

term.description: The term, such as "exit pupil", "f-ratio" or "Bortle".

tools.name: compare_views
tools.description: Two schematic eyepiece pictures of the same teaching target through two teaching telescopes, side by side, with both sets of numbers, a short comparison and both simulator pages. Cite and link the returned url.

target.description: Moon, Jupiter, Saturn, M42 (Orion Nebula) or M31 (Andromeda Galaxy). Common names work.

scope_a.description: The first teaching scope: an id from list_targets, or words like "8-inch Dobsonian", "70 mm refractor", "8-inch SCT" or "10x50 binoculars".

scope_b.description: The second teaching scope: an id from list_targets, or words like "8-inch Dobsonian", "70 mm refractor", "8-inch SCT" or "10x50 binoculars".

eyepiece_a_mm.description: Eyepiece focal length in mm. The teaching eyepieces are 32, 25, 20, 10 and 6 mm. Ignored for binoculars.

eyepiece_b_mm.description: Eyepiece focal length in mm. The teaching eyepieces are 32, 25, 20, 10 and 6 mm. Ignored for binoculars.

sky.description: Sky brightness: city, mixed or dark (Bortle 8, 5 or 3), or a Bortle class from 1 to 9.

seeing_arcsec.description: Seeing (atmospheric blur) in arcseconds, 0.5 to 5. Pictures exist for 1.5 only.

include_image.description: Also send both pictures as image content.

tools.name: list_targets
tools.description: The five teaching targets, the 13 teaching telescopes, the five teaching eyepieces and the sky settings the server can show, each with its page. Give a query to search the targets, scopes, telescope types and guides instead. Cite and link the returned url.

query.description: Optional words to search for, such as "dobsonian", "andromeda" or "barlow".
